name: OwnerAction_DiffSlots
domain: Compares two 32-entry OwnerActionSlot arrays (struct OwnerActionSlot { u16 encoded_action; u16 unknown_02; }, the same action_slots vocabulary owner/action/add.c and include/owner_state.h already use at offset 0x58 of struct OwnerActionState). For every non-zero entry of the second array (b) it writes the masked key (& 0x3fff) into an output u16 array and, if that key is not found anywhere in the first array (a, scanned up to 32 entries), ORs in flag 0x8000 and counts it. It then does the mirror pass over a against b, appending (key & 0x3fff) | 0x4000 for every a-entry not found in b. Returns the total entries written; *lost_count gets the 0x8000 count, *(stack arg 5) gets the 0x4000 count. This is a leaf function (no bl instructions) so it has no callees to corroborate via shared call targets.
notes: The family-matcher's best guess (games/gs1/src/ui/window/clear_tile_attributes_in_rect.c, 7482/10000, below this project's 7500 threshold) was checked directly and is a shape-only match: same register-shuffle prologue as many UI-window owners in this address neighborhood, but its actual body (a nested row/column tile-rect clear using masks 0x3FF/0xFC) shares no callee, field offset, or constant with this owner. Rejected as unrelated, per this session's brief that above-threshold matches in this cluster were majority false positives for the same reason.

Real evidence instead came from hand-tracing games/gs1/asm/080aae14.s (no callees; parameters recovered purely from register roles) plus a grep for the mask constant 0x3fff across games/gs1/src: games/gs1/src/owner/action/add.c (OwnerAction_Add, Func_08078e28) declares the exact same 4-byte-stride record ({u16 value; u16 padding;}, masked with 0x3fff) at owner-state offset 0x58, and games/gs1/include/owner_state.h already promotes that vocabulary to struct OwnerActionSlot/struct OwnerActionState with LAYOUT_OFFSET_GUARD-verified offsets. All three real callers (games/gs1/asm/080ad6d4.s, 080acab8.s, 080ae2f4.s -- none yet adopted) pass pointers of the form ownerBase+88 (0x58) for the first two arguments, confirming both pointer parameters are struct OwnerActionSlot* views into two different (or, in one 080ae2f4.s call site, the same) owners' action_slots. m2c's independent decompilation of the retained assembly against the real agscc type context (out/workbench/080aae14/m2c/080aae14.c) reproduced the same two-loop, same-mask, same-flag-bit shape from the raw instructions alone, corroborating the hand trace.

The neighboring already-registered owner main:080ae9f0 (UiIcon_DrawVariantWithTileOffset, icon/marker drawing) is called from the same caller as this owner (games/gs1/asm/080acab8.s) but is semantically unrelated to the action-slot diff itself; it is only useful as evidence that this caller's scene mixes icon drawing with an action-list comparison, consistent with a class-change/ability-list preview screen. No stronger name for the screen itself is claimed.

Iterated the source shape extensively against tools/compiler/target/release/compiler candidate-show --align: the initial index-only draft scored differing_halfwords=154/wrong_instructions=192. Replacing the two 32-entry linear searches with an explicit pointer walk (struct OwnerActionSlot *p; do { cnt++; if (cnt>31) break; p++; } while (masked-xor != 0);) -- matching the reference's genuine incrementing-pointer inner loops instead of index*4 addressing -- was the single largest improvement, to differing_halfwords=113/wrong_instructions=122 (candidate_bytes=324, exactly matching owner_bytes=324; candidate_insns=149 == reference_insns=149 per --asm). The final structural workbench report (out/workbench/080aae14/structural.json) scores this 91.79% match_percent: 85/160 instructions byte-identical, and only 8 true insertions/deletions/opcode/replacement differences -- the rest (65) are argument-only (register-number) mismatches.

The remaining 8 structural instructions cluster in two places, both downstream of one register-allocation choice: the reference keeps the second parameter (b) resident in r8 for the whole function (mov r8,r1 as the very first body instruction) and reuses that same r0/r8 pair as a single raw pointer for both loop1's per-entry loads and its 32-entry bound test (mov r3,r8; adds r3,#124; cmp r0,r3). This draft's compiled output instead lands b in r9, promotes a transient copy of the out-pointer into r8 inside loop1, and expresses loop1's bound test as an index compare (movs r4,#1; add r8,r4 as a counter; cmp r2,#31) rather than the reference's pointer-vs-base+124 compare -- a second, coupled residual. Tried and rejected: an explicit `struct OwnerActionSlot *bp = b` alias (no change -- compiler already treats it identically to the parameter); reordering the lost++/flag-OR statement pair to match the reference's exact instruction order (no change -- already schedules identically); splitting the single shared `i` loop counter into distinct `i`/`j` per loop (differing_halfwords improved to 98 and wrong_instructions to 117, but the candidate shrank to 318 bytes -- gained/lost migrated out of their stack slots into extra registers, changing the frame from `sub sp,#12` to `sub sp,#8` and losing matched_prefix; rejected as a worse structural match despite the lower raw diff count, restored the shared-index draft); converting loop1's outer walk to a fully pointer-based `do { ...; bp++; } while ((u8*)bp <= (u8*)b+124 && ...)` to mirror the reference's unified pointer directly (regressed to differing_halfwords=131/wrong_instructions=176 and dropped matched_prefix to 7 -- rejected, restored the index-based draft). No PERM_GENERAL/PERM_INT permutation, register hint, inline asm, or compiler-flag change was used; the residual is treated as a register-allocation-sensitive gap under CONTRIBUTING's 'invert a stalled last mile' guidance, not yet resolved by source respelling alone.
Not adopted (differing_halfwords=113, not zero). Kept as the closest measured draft. No cross-edition comparison was performed this session.
